nodes.title: Provided hourly data
nodes.subtitle: National + twelve regional series
nodes.description: National consumption is the target in every comparison. Regional demand and temperature are predictors, not replacement evaluation truth. There is no regional RTE forecast. Raw observations remain unchanged.

nodes.title: Forecast contract
nodes.subtitle: 11:00 Paris on D → all hours of D+1
nodes.description: Cutoff-aware history, explicit publication-delay assumptions and 23/24/25-hour local delivery days. An 11:00 Europe/Paris origin is also before a literal 12:00 fixed-CET deadline in summer. Later studies use separate versioned configurations.

nodes.title: Vintage archive schemas
nodes.subtitle: Demand revisions · RTE issues · weather
nodes.description: The supplied archives contain headers only. They define interfaces, not authentic historical observations or forecast runs. RTE D1 availability is assumed; no D2 timing rule is used.

nodes.title: Operational evidence unavailable
nodes.subtitle: Retrospective results; exposed test period
nodes.description: No identified future-label leak does not establish authentic historical input availability. Original forecast vintages, demand revisions and source-to-hourly aggregation are unverified. The test period was previously explored. No operational validation or euro savings claim follows.

nodes.title: Integrity and artifact checks
nodes.subtitle: Tests + hashes + daily-origin ledgers
nodes.description: Behavioral tests and saved-artifact audits cover availability, leakage, DST, complete intervals, reproducibility, frozen identities, matched arithmetic and executed notebooks. Recorded verification is evidence for this run, not a forecast-vintage guarantee.

nodes.title: 01  Data audit
nodes.subtitle: Dictionary, availability, reconciliation
nodes.description: Audit original values, overlap, missingness and hourly conventions; record assumptions and source fingerprints.

nodes.title: 02  Development EDA
nodes.subtitle: Calendar, temperature, RTE errors
nodes.description: Development-only patterns and observation counts support a hypothesis register.

nodes.title: 03  Replay and baselines
nodes.subtitle: Origin → delivery interval
nodes.description: Cutoff-eligible features, labels stored separately and common baseline replay.

nodes.title: 04  Model comparison
nodes.subtitle: Validate → select → freeze
nodes.description: Earlier compact candidate/feature comparison with chronological validation and declared fallback policies.

nodes.title: 05  Uncertainty and failures
nodes.subtitle: Intervals, matched scores, bootstrap
nodes.description: Earlier frozen-policy evaluation and past-error uncertainty diagnostics.

nodes.title: 06  Research recommendation
nodes.subtitle: Scorecard, limitations, business meaning
nodes.description: Filename retained for links. This notebook reports research evidence and limitations; it does not implement deployment or monitoring.

nodes.title: Legacy 02 investigation
nodes.subtitle: Separate notebook; separate evaluation protocol
nodes.description: Historical baseline investigation. It is not the canonical notebook 02 and does not define the later origin-aware comparison protocol.

nodes.title: Shared original research modules
nodes.subtitle: Audit · features · replay · metrics · uncertainty
nodes.description: Reusable original workflow implementation. Availability, calendar/DST, fallback, matching and scoring helpers are also imported by later research modules.

nodes.title: Original workflow artifacts
nodes.subtitle: Audit, hypotheses, feature store and scorecards
nodes.description: Earlier workflow evidence is preserved. Do not confuse its frozen candidate or scores with any later versioned study.

nodes.title: 07  Statistical and boosting models
nodes.subtitle: Original study + two RTE extensions
nodes.description: Orchestrates statistical and tabular experiments, then preserves appended RTE-assisted and expanded-feature/cold-risk sections.

nodes.title: 08  Deep learning and uncertainty
nodes.subtitle: Neural comparisons + probabilistic evaluation
nodes.description: Resumes the original research study, compares neural candidates and evaluates separately identified uncertainty methods. Appended sections report later RTE extensions.

nodes.title: Notebook and run tooling
nodes.subtitle: Author / extend / execute / verify
nodes.description: Authoring scripts serve different notebook generations; extension scripts preserve earlier study sections. The risk runner performs prepare, development, evaluation and report stages. Viewing this graph does not execute these scripts.

nodes.title: Original research_v2
nodes.subtitle: 13 families · 23 variants + four references
nodes.description: Original bounded statistical, boosting and neural comparison; national and regional-assisted histories. Its development-selected complete policy was rolling RTE bias correction. Finite neural budgets and training-anchor limitations constrain architecture comparisons.

nodes.title: First RTE-assisted study
nodes.subtitle: 16 tabular variants; direct versus residual
nodes.description: Extends ResearchRun with RTE predictors. Residual target = actual − RTE; prediction = RTE + learned correction. Its old regional arm includes national plus regional history. This is not the new regional-only arm.

nodes.title: Expanded risk specification
nodes.subtitle: 55 new variants; four development folds
nodes.description: Q2–Q4 2024 and Q1 2025 development; April–June 2025 calibration; previously explored July 2025–June 2026 evaluation. Weighted-MAE selection penalizes realized cold evenings fivefold. Three predictor views and 23 labeled hybrids; all base architectures were not natively retrained with RTE.

nodes.title: Three causal predictor views
nodes.subtitle: National / regional-only / combined
nodes.description: Every view predicts national demand and includes calendar plus assumed-known RTE D1. Regional-only excludes national demand, temperature and error histories. Origin/delivery lags, rolling statistics, EWMA, changes, RTE errors and delivery-day RTE shape respect declared availability. Future realized weather is excluded.

nodes.title: Chronological learned features
nodes.subtitle: Ridge demand + two logistic probabilities
nodes.description: Monthly earlier-data fits produce out-of-sample demand, cold probability and large RTE-underprediction probability. Training labels must be released before fitting; preprocessing is fitted within eligible history. Predicted cold probability can weight training.

nodes.title: Causal base forecasts / hybrids
nodes.subtitle: 23 archived base variants; new LGBM combiner
nodes.description: Original out-of-sample model predictions are selected using released earlier-quarter outcomes, then supplied to a new LightGBM RTE-residual combiner. A hybrid represents the original family as an input forecast; it is not native RTE-feature retraining of that architecture.

nodes.title: RiskLabRun replay and selection
nodes.subtitle: Train → predict → seal → score → freeze
nodes.description: Quarterly point-model refits; released-label training; complete daily origins. Native tabular variants and hybrids share the replay. Point selection uses development weighted MAE plus availability/ordinary-MAE/cold-MAE guardrails. Forecast files omit outcomes and carry hashes and per-origin ledgers.

nodes.title: Selected point policy
nodes.subtitle: Combined + learned; neutral training weights
nodes.description: lab__lightgbm__combined__stacked__w1__residual. RTE plus a learned correction, selected on cold-weighted development loss. Neutral training weights won this bounded comparison. Its empirical residual intervals are evaluated as a separate uncertainty construction.

nodes.title: Separate quantile selection
nodes.subtitle: Combined + learned; cold-probability weights
nodes.description: lab__lightgbm_quantile__combined__stacked__w5__residual. Chosen by overall development WIS, not best cold coverage. Quantile grid supports central/asymmetric intervals; sorted crossing repair is predeclared. Do not attach its metrics to the selected point policy.

nodes.title: Fixed calibration comparators
nodes.subtitle: Engineered-only native / split / CQR
nodes.description: Separately fixed predictor before calibration, excluding monthly learned-input updates. Split-conformal and CQR produce calibrated bounds, not guaranteed conditional quantiles. Calibration contains zero cold evenings; time dependence and regime shift preclude automatic coverage guarantees.

nodes.title: Matched scores and uncertainty
nodes.subtitle: MAE, cold loss, pinball, WIS, CRPS, blocks
nodes.description: Exactly matched observations, paired day-block intervals, feature ablations and directional tail failures. CRPS is a score; conformal is calibration. Marginal hourly intervals do not define daily energy/peak intervals. Physical-unit risk scenarios do not measure euro savings.

nodes.title: Saved predictions and provenance
nodes.subtitle: Forecasts · fit logs · ledgers · source hashes
nodes.description: Frozen run artifacts preserve predictions before outcomes, fitting availability and source/raw identities. Reports reuse these saved outputs; graph generation never fits models.

nodes.title: Descriptive failure diagnostics
nodes.subtitle: Monthly/hourly errors; worst cold-day trajectory
nodes.description: Reporting-only reconstruction from saved forecasts and raw outcomes: counts, signed errors, missing-target exclusion, worst days and interval failures. Measured cold/calendar conditions are not proof of weather forecast misses or causal explanations.

nodes.title: Written manager recommendation
nodes.subtitle: Three questions; eight exportable figures
nodes.description: 1. Improvement over RTE. 2. Uncertainty and failures. 3. Recommendation and risks. Distinguishes measured retrospective gains from inadequate cold-tail coverage, vintage uncertainty, exposed test history and national-to-portfolio limitations.

nodes.title: Interactive manager report
nodes.subtitle: Reviewed snapshot → report app
nodes.description: Local report app presents frozen comparisons, diagnostics and inspectable provenance. Its hypothetical point-forecast penalty chart differs from the written report’s quantile-decision scenario. Neither establishes financial savings; neither is a production forecasting service.

module_summary.docstring:
Shared evaluation module for the electricity demand forecasting project.

Every model notebook (naive baseline, SARIMAX, LightGBM, probabilistic intervals,
final comparison, ...) imports from here instead of redefining its own data
loading, train/test splits, or metrics. That's the whole point of this module:
if each notebook rolled its own splits or metric formulas, results across models
would not be a fair comparison. By sharing `load_data`, `walk_forward_folds`,
the metric functions, and `save_result`, every `results/<model>.json` file is
directly comparable to every other one.

Validation standard implemented here: walk-forward, quarterly, expanding (or
optionally sliding) window over the test year 2025-07-01 -> 2026-06-30, split
into 4 quarterly folds. See readme.md for the full rationale.

definitions.name: load_data
definitions.docstring:
Load the hourly France electricity CSV, convert to Europe/Paris local time.

Parses `datetime_utc`, converts to `Europe/Paris`, sorts chronologically, names
the index `datetime_local`, and drops the 7 rows with NaN load/RTE forecast at
the autumn DST transition each year.

definitions.name: score
definitions.docstring: Align two series, drop unpaired/NaN rows, return MAE/RMSE/MAPE dict.

definitions.name: walk_forward_folds
definitions.docstring:
Yield (fold_idx, train, test) over the 4 fixed quarterly folds.

Test region: 2025-07-01 -> 2026-06-30, split into 4 quarterly folds:
  fold 1: train <= 2025-06-30 23:00, test = Jul-Sep 2025
  fold 2: train <= 2025-09-30 23:00, test = Oct-Dec 2025
  fold 3: train <= 2025-12-31 23:00, test = Jan-Mar 2026
  fold 4: train <= 2026-03-31 23:00, test = Apr-Jun 2026

window="expanding": train is everything in `df` from its start up to the
fold's train-end timestamp (inclusive).
window="sliding": train is only the last `window_size` (a pandas.Timedelta,
or a number of hours) ending at the same train-end timestamp.

definitions.name: save_result
definitions.docstring:
Save per-fold metrics plus their mean/std to results/<name>.json.

`fold_results` is a list of dicts, one per fold, each shaped like:
    {"fold": 1, "train_start": ..., "train_end": ..., "test_start": ...,
     "test_end": ..., "metrics": {"MAE_MW": ..., "RMSE_MW": ..., "MAPE_pct": ...}}

definitions.name: threshold_weighted_empirical_crps
definitions.docstring:
Exact upper-tail twCRPS for an equally weighted empirical residual CDF.

The weight is 1{x >= threshold}. CRPS after clipping both the outcome and
every ensemble member below at threshold equals this weighted integral.
Prefix sums evaluate that exact discrete-distribution score in O(n log n)
preprocessing and O(log n) per forecast, without constructing a huge matrix.

module_summary.docstring:
Small, auditable model adapters for the research notebooks.

This module does not split data, select hyperparameters, or know evaluation
outcomes. The replay engine must supply only information released before each
forecast origin. In particular, ``fit`` never performs a random validation split.

The GAM is a penalized additive B-spline regression, implemented with sklearn.
It is not advertised as pyGAM: smoothing is Ridge's alpha and must be selected
with external chronological validation. No cross-feature interactions are added.

definitions.name: parameter_grid
definitions.docstring:
Return bounded, deterministic candidates; never use test-set information.

``fast`` gives two configurations per family. Statistical fast candidates
include explicit 56/84-day windows and iteration caps for bounded CPU cost;
these do not establish optimally tuned statistical performance.
``full`` is a modest expansion
(8 statistical and 12 tabular configurations), not an exhaustive search.

module_summary.docstring:
Official NeuralForecast adapters for the research benchmark.

The six architectures are Nixtla implementations, pinned to NeuralForecast 1.7.7
for this Intel Mac's PyTorch 2.2.2. No fallback architecture is substituted.
The forecast-origin engine, not this adapter, is responsible for publication
delays, eligible history, delivery-day selection, and origin-based outer scoring.

All variants here deliberately use target history only. Global panel fitting is
shared-parameter univariate learning, not explicit cross-region multivariate
learning. Each call predicts ``h`` consecutive UTC hours after the context end;
the engine must select tomorrow's 23/24/25 actual delivery intervals.

Missing training observations remain on the grid with ``available_mask=0`` and
are excluded from normalization statistics/loss. Predictor placeholders use only
the previous observed value within that series; leading gaps use zero. This is
explicit causal input imputation, with no backward fill or target interpolation.
The caller's evaluation truth remains unchanged and missing targets stay excluded.

Upstream sources (versioned):
https://github.com/Nixtla/neuralforecast/tree/v1.7.7/neuralforecast/models
https://github.com/Nixtla/neuralforecast/blob/v1.7.7/neuralforecast/core.py
https://github.com/Nixtla/neuralforecast/blob/v1.7.7/settings.ini

Matched point scores, honest empirical distributions and frozen conformal.

CRPS is computed for a fully specified empirical residual distribution. Native
three-quantile forecasts receive pinball/interval scores, not invented CRPS.

module_summary.docstring:
Chronological RTE-assisted extension; preserves the original frozen experiment.

Direct demand prediction with RTE predictors and residual learning are distinct
predeclared variants. Both receive identical predictors and fallback rules.
Only tabular adapters are supported; no neural architecture is substituted.

Causal, already-out-of-sample base forecasts for RTE feature stacking.

The original benchmark contains both candidate configurations in every 2024
quarter. Selecting its full-year winner inside that same year's stacker would
leak model-selection information. This bank instead starts with trial 0, then
selects each later quarter using only earlier-quarter outcomes released before
that quarter's first forecast origin. January 2025 freezes the full-2024 winner,
which must match the original run before its calibration/test forecasts are used.

This is an explicitly two-stage hybrid feature bank. It does not claim that
N-BEATS, PatchTST, ARIMA, or any other base model gained native exogenous inputs.
No fitting, raw-data mutation, or source-artifact mutation occurs here.

definitions.name: select_released_trial
definitions.docstring:
Select from externally supplied OOS trials using strictly released labels.

The caller supplies only previous-quarter predictions. Rows at or after the
selection origin are additionally excluded. Availability follows the original
benchmark: raw predictions on nonmissing eligible evaluation targets.

definitions.name: causal_quarter_stream
definitions.docstring:
Return one variant's 2024 OOS stream and its causal selection ledger.

``quarter_trials`` is an ordered sequence of (quarter_name, {trial: frame}).
Q1 is fixed-trial burn-in, suitable for training later stacker folds only.

definitions.name: load_causal_base_bank
definitions.docstring:
Return (wide origin-delivery base features, selection ledger).

The ledger is a JSON-serializable dictionary containing quarterly selections,
final-selection agreement, every referenced artifact hash, and arm semantics.
No observed outcomes enter the returned wide feature table.

module_summary.docstring:
Causal feature laboratory for the RTE D1-assisted retrospective experiment.

``rte_forecast_d1_mw`` is assumed available at the configured origin. Its missing
issue-time lineage is not repaired by this module. Historical actuals and weather
must pass the interval-end plus publication-delay gate. Rolling averages here are
observed-history summaries, not fitted ARIMA moving-average innovations.

definitions.name: _series_features
definitions.docstring: All origin lags refer to an exact UTC hour, never the last nonmissing row.

definitions.name: build_lab_origin_features
definitions.docstring:
Build one complete 23/24/25-hour target day with a fixed pre-noon origin.

RTE profile transforms use this delivery day's supplied D1 values only.
Regional observations have the same explicit assumed delay as national data.
This is not an archived-vintage operational reconstruction.

definitions.name: FeatureLabData

definitions.name: feature_register

module_summary.docstring:
Fixed, chronological first-stage predictions for the RTE feature laboratory.

Every bank value is a prediction from a model fitted before that value's
forecast origin. There are no fitted training predictions in the bank. These
models are deliberately fixed rather than selected using development/test
scores. National future temperature is a released training label for the cold
classifier, including in the regional-only arm; it is never an input feature.

definitions.name: _fit_component
definitions.signature: _fit_component(training, prediction, columns, target, released_at, origin, *, classification)
definitions.docstring: Return honest predictions and auditable metadata, including one-class fits.

definitions.name: build_learned_feature_bank
definitions.docstring:
Return origin/delivery keys plus three chronological predictors per arm.

The optional cache is addressed by source, raw-data, engineered-feature,
label and fixed-specification hashes. ``result.attrs['fit_ledger']`` records
every monthly component fit. A temperature label without its own release
timestamp uses the supplied demand release assumption explicitly; that
assumption does not establish historical publication vintages.

The input data object and its predictor columns are not modified. All rows
retain their historical origin, including 23/25-hour daylight-saving days.
Missing warm-up predictions remain missing for downstream fold-fitted
imputation; no future fit is used to backfill them.

definitions.name: predicted_cold_evening_weights
definitions.docstring:
Point-loss training weights from original-origin cold predictions only.

Missing warm-up probabilities receive neutral weight one. These weights
emphasize forecast cold evenings without looking at realized future cold
conditions. They are not a settlement-cost estimate and should not be used
as outcome-dependent weighting of a nominal quantile distribution.

definitions.name: empirical_intervals

Rolling signed out-of-sample errors available strictly before each origin.

Earlier test observations may enter the predeclared online calibration policy.
No in-sample training residuals or future outcomes enter a calibration pool.

definitions.name: trajectory_intervals
definitions.docstring:
Resample complete daily residual vectors; match 23/24/25-hour length.

These are empirical scenarios, not simultaneous-coverage guarantees. DST
lengths with insufficient complete historical days explicitly remain missing.
